Topic:Cricket

Litchfield's quick fire 50 helped the Australians to a commanding victory in Brisbane. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris)

Australia defeated Bangladesh by seven wickets to take a 1-0 lead in the ODI series in Brisbane.

Opening batter Phoebe Litchfield struck 77 from 57 deliveries as the hosts chased down their target of 167 in just 25.4 overs.

The series will continue on Sunday and then finish on Wednesday, with both the second and third ODIs also to be played at Allan Border Field.

A Phoebe Litchfield masterclass has ensured Australia remains undefeated in 22 ODIs at Allan Border Field after seamer Megan Schutt joined an elite club of bowling greats.

Opener Litchfield's 77 off 57 deliveries ensured Australia polished off the meagre 166 all out set by Bangladesh in just 25.4 overs for the loss of three wickets.

Litchfield combined ramps, glides, clips, exquisite drives, lofted pitching wedges, reverse hockey thumps and thunderous wallops in another knock that confirmed she is unique in world cricket and an absolute joy to watch.

The left-hander was unstoppable in racing to her 12th ODI half-century.

All-rounder Annabel Sutherland, player of the match, finished the chase with 26 not out after earlier taking four wickets.

Australia pace bowler Schutt earlier snared her 150th ODI wicket in a probing opening spell to put the hosts on top.

Stand-in captain Tahlia McGrath invited the visitors to have first use of the surface and Schutt struck with the first ball of the innings, a vicious lifter that had opener Fargana Hoque edging to slip.

A Schutt inswinger trapped Sarmin Sultana (four) in front and from that moment the bowlers kept a vice-like grip on the run rate and picked up steady wickets to dismiss Bangladesh with the fourth ball of the final over.

The wicket of Sultana was the milestone 150th for Schutt. Only legendary speed demon Cathryn Fitzpatrick (180) and current all-rounder Ellyse Perry (166) have more wickets for Australia in the format.

Schutt finished with 2-19 from her 10 overs with medium pacer Sutherland (4-30) proving a handful when she hit the pitch hard.

Spinners Ashleigh Gardner, Georgia Wareham and Alana King bowled with class.

The visitors had several cameos but nothing substantial. No.3 Sharmin Akhter made a classy and breezy 24, captain Nigar Sultana (29 off 86 balls) was brave but stodgy.

Veteran all-rounder Ritu Moni (45 off 63) showcased her experience and nous and was the best of a mediocre bunch.

Schutt has relished playing at AB Field throughout her career, where she now has 20 wickets.

The quick was initially left out of the ODI side in February against India before a quad injury to Kim Garth opened the door for a recall.

Schutt took 5-19 at AB Field on that occasion to provide a timely reminder of her talents.

McGrath, usually a vice-captain, has been elevated to lead due to injury to regular skipper Sophie Molineux and rotated her bowlers with panache.

The opener of three ODIs at the same venue, Friday's clash is the first match of the summer on home soil for Australia's victorious T20 World Cup side since lifting the trophy in July.
